Crash.Suggestion.InvalidModFileName: Remove or rename the affected mod file so that its name contains only English letters, numbers, hyphens, underscores, and periods.
Crash.Suggestion.JavaIncompatible: Choose a suitable Java version in launch settings based on the Minecraft version and mod requirements.
Crash.Suggestion.JavaTooNew: Switch to an older Java version in launch settings and try again.

Crash.Suggestion.OldForgeNewJavaIncompat: Try updating Forge or switching to an older Java version.

Crash.Suggestion.OptiFineForgeIncompatib: Check the compatible OptiFine and Forge versions, then reinstall matching versions.
Crash.Suggestion.OptiFineWorldLoadCrash: Try another OptiFine version, or remove OptiFine before entering the world again.

Crash.Suggestion.ResourcePackTooLarge: Remove high-resolution resource packs or lower their resolution. You can also update the graphics driver.
Crash.Suggestion.ShadersModWithOptiFine: Remove Shaders Mod. OptiFine already provides shader support.

Crash.Suggestion.StackKeyword: Check the mods or libraries related to these keywords. You can also export the crash report for more details.
Crash.Suggestion.TooManyModsIdLimit: Reduce the number of installed mods, or install a fix mod that extends the ID limit for older Minecraft versions.
Crash.Suggestion.UsingJdk: Switch to a regular JRE or another Java version that is suitable for this instance in launch settings.
Crash.Suggestion.UsingOpenJ9: Switch to HotSpot Java in launch settings and try again.
Crash.Suggestion.ViewReport: View the crash report for more details about how the error happened.
Crash.Suggestion.X86JavaMemoryLimit.OnX6: Install and select 64-bit Java in launch settings, then try again.

Instance.Setup.Advanced.PreLaunchCommand:
This does not override the global setting: the global command runs first, then the instance command.

Executes a command or program before launching Minecraft, using Windows command prompt syntax.

The following substitution tokens can be used for relative paths (paths end with \):
 · {path}: PCL-Anywhere executable folder
 · {minecraft}: .minecraft folder
 · {verpath}: Instance folder (.minecraft\versions\instance-name\)
 · {verindie}: Version folder when isolation is on, .minecraft folder otherwise
 · {java}: Java runtime folder

Additionally, these tokens are also supported:
 · {user}: Player name
 · {login}: Player login method
 · {uuid}: Player UUID
 · {name}: Game instance name
 · {date}, {time}: Current system time
 · {version}: Game vanilla version

Examples:
 · "{verpath}test.exe" : Run test.exe in the instance folder
 · "{java}java.exe" -jar "{verpath}test.jar" : Run test.jar from the instance folder with Java
 · notepad "{verindie}options.txt" : Open the instance settings file with Notepad

Always wrap paths in double quotes to avoid failures caused by spaces.
The working directory when executing the command is the current .minecraft folder.

- Launcher version information and identifier
- Windows system version and architecture
- Installed physical memory size
- NAT and IPv6 support status

This data is not associated with you, and we will never sell it to any third party.
If you do not want to enable telemetry, you can choose to decline. This will not affect normal use of other features, but may affect developers' ability to fix potential bugs.

Setup.Launch.Advanced.LockMemory.ToolTip: When enabled, the launcher additionally appends -Xms equal to the maximum heap (-Xmx), fixing the heap size. The trade-off is that the game holds close to the maximum allocated memory for its entire runtime.

Setup.Launch.Advanced.PreLaunchCommand.T:
Execute a specific command or program before Minecraft launches. The syntax is the same as Windows Command Prompt.

The following replacement tokens can be used for relative paths (paths all end with \):
 · {path}: The folder containing PCL-Anywhere's exe file
 · {minecraft}: The .minecraft folder
 · {verpath}: Instance folder (.minecraft\versions\instance_name\)
 · {verindie}: Same as the instance folder when instance isolation is enabled; otherwise same as the .minecraft folder
 · {java}: The Java folder used by the game

The following replacement tokens are also supported:
 · {user}: Username
 · {login}: Login method
 · {uuid}: Player UUID
 · {name}: Instance name
 · {date}, {time}: System time
 · {version}: Vanilla game version

Examples:
 · "{verpath}test.exe": Run test.exe in the instance folder
 · "{java}java.exe" -jar "{verpath}test.jar": Use Java to run test.jar in the instance folder
 · notepad "{verindie}options.txt": Open the instance settings file with Notepad

It is recommended to wrap paths in double quotes to avoid launch failures caused by spaces in the path.
When the command is executed, the working directory is the current .minecraft folder.
